content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese with reduced lactose is a dairy product made from skimmed milk in which most of the lactose has been removed. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor, a soft curdled texture and low calorie content, making it popular among weight‑watchers and people sensitive to lactose.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, known already in ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat versions contain about 90 % water, making them lighter than regular cottage cheese.
Lactose reduction is achieved by enzymatic hydrolysis, splitting lactose into glucose and galactose.
Cottage cheese is widely used in cheese‑nibbles, baked dishes and diet desserts.
In some countries the product is called “cottage cheese,” although texture may vary slightly.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Fat usually does not exceed 1 %, making it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Reduced lactose
items.content: The lower lactose level eases digestion for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: It supplies about 10 % of the daily calcium requirement, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties are salted, so sodium intake should be monitored.

items.title: Processing quality
items.content: Low‑quality products may harbor microbial contamination; choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be enjoyed as a snack, blended into smoothies, added to salads, used as a filling for pancakes, casseroles and diet desserts. It pairs well with berries, nuts or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, keep for 5–7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
